stage: Canonical remaster, actual ImageGen concept and independent imported GLB feedback reviewed

iterations.prompt: Create a high-quality 3D game-asset concept of the Mauna Type3 cargo transport in the attached archival pixel-art reference. The reference determines the silhouette and grey/pale-blue material pattern. A broad chamfered horizontal lower housing carries THREE tall thin vertical rectangular sections, arranged along its length with large open gaps between sections. Each section has three deep rectangular notches opening out of the same edge, like a thick comb; notches are real open recesses rather than dark painted squares. Three sections have approximately equal manufactured height; small apparent differences in the tiny oblique reference may be perspective. Pale blue-grey opaque metal bands across their grey faces and across the lower housing. A few warm brown metal feet under the base, two small grey underside blocks, restrained brown end fittings. End view is narrow, with one tall section hiding the other two; broadside view shows all three spaced sections. Use the distinctive unusual reference shape, not a conventional streamlined ship. Hidden geometry and recess depth remain interpretation, not exact recovered engineering. Sparse fitted service panels, small fasteners and shallow maintenance seams; broad quiet surfaces without dense grid subdivisions. Used utilitarian metal with restrained grime at joins, stains, scratches, scuffs and small dents, retaining clear edges. No added glass, glowing parts, text, logo, extra appendages or equipment. One large elevated three-quarter view and smaller consistent broadside/end views of exactly the same assembly. Charcoal studio background, no captions.

input_images.role: Actual paletted legacy primary shape and colour evidence

iterations.verdict: Useful coherent three-section notched assembly, pale band continuation, broad lower casing and warm feet. Equal section heights and exact full-width recesses remain interpretation; do not infer unequal towers from perspective. Concept panels/hidden connections are artistic guidance, not exact source geometry.
